findings.title: Same service ownership story repeated across three sections

evidence.notes: The same service set (simpleDataService, cachedDataService, supabaseService, validation) is listed repeatedly with near-identical wording.

findings.risk: Edits can update one section and miss others, creating internal documentation drift.

canonicalSource.recommendation: Keep a single "Data flow" section in ARCHITECTURE and treat ownership bullets as references, not repeated definitions.

findings.title: Documented dual-facade runtime vs observed primary runtime

evidence.notes: Architecture presents simple and cached facades as peers. Current UI imports simpleDataService; cached facade appears non-primary in active runtime entrypoint.

findings.risk: Behavior and error semantics can diverge if both facades evolve independently.

canonicalSource.recommendation: Declare one canonical runtime facade and mark the other as experimental/deprecated or internal.

findings.title: Auth/session pipeline repeated in flow, ownership, and hotspot sections

evidence.notes: AuthProvider + sessionValidationService + validate/refresh routes + proxy are restated multiple times.

findings.risk: Retry/state-machine changes are likely to be reflected inconsistently across sections.

canonicalSource.recommendation: Keep one authoritative state-machine section and link to it from ownership/hotspot sections.

findings.title: Cache architecture repeated with overlapping terms

evidence.notes: The same cache components are described repeatedly with slightly different language (cache, invalidation, service worker).

findings.risk: Terminology drift (what is cached where) can hide invalidation bugs.

canonicalSource.recommendation: Define a single cache semantics table (scope, store, TTL, invalidation trigger) and reference it everywhere else.

findings.title: Preference schema changed quickly; narrative can lag migrations

evidence.notes: Recent preference migrations indicate active schema churn; static prose is prone to lag behind current column defaults/meaning.

findings.risk: Doc readers may implement against stale defaults or field expectations.

canonicalSource.recommendation: Treat migrations as source of truth; keep only high-level intent in ARCHITECTURE and auto-generate a schema appendix where possible.

findings.title: Encryption implementation references span RPC and client fallback paths

evidence.notes: The architecture text explains dual-path encryption behavior; these paths are sensitive to SQL function revisions and fallback behavior changes.

findings.risk: Security assumptions in docs can become stale without immediate code or migration updates.

canonicalSource.recommendation: Keep ARCHITECTURE at policy level (what must hold) and defer algorithm/runtime specifics to privacyService + SQL migration comments.

findings.title: Hotspot list duplicates ownership map instead of adding unique risk data

evidence.notes: Hotspots mostly re-list the same files from ownership sections with descriptive prose.

findings.risk: Low signal-to-noise; reviewers skip the section and miss real risk deltas.

canonicalSource.recommendation: Convert hotspots into measurable metrics (change frequency, defect density, coupling) instead of repeated inventory.
